samples.summary: New style-normalization boundary treats only `''` specially and performs no validation of the color value it lets through; defense-in-depth would reject non-color strings at the write boundary rather than relying solely on export-time sanitizers
samples.evidence: `normalizeStyleClears` / `normalizeCellStyleClears` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:271-309) rewrite the `''` sentinel but pass any other string through verbatim into the CRDT attribute (`serializeCellStyle` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:235 writes `s.backgroundColor` unchanged; `applyStyleInTree` at :1921 likewise). I traced every downstream sink I could find and all of them are safe today: canvas paint goes through `resolveStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:47) into `ctx.fillStyle` (no script/CSS context), DOCX/PPTX attributes go through `toRgbHexColor` which returns only `[0-9A-F]{6}` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:113 — 'injection-proof by construction'), and PDF export narrows to numeric channels via `styleColor` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-style-map.ts:151). I found no `innerHTML` / `cssText` / stylesheet sink that consumes a docs color, so I could not complete an exploit chain — hence low confidence and nit severity. The residual risk is only that a future HTML/CSS/SVG sink would inherit an unvalidated persisted value.
searchedFor: Grep `resolveStoredColor|toRgbHexColor` across the repo to enumerate color sinks
Read yorkie-doc-store.ts serializeCellStyle / removedCellStyleAttrs / removeNodeStyle / applyStyleInTree / applyCellStyle

finding.summary: DOCX export still interpolates `style.alignment` into a `w:val` attribute unescaped — the same XML-attribute-injection class this delta just closed for colors
finding.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` emits `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:106-109) with `align` taken verbatim from `BlockStyle.alignment`. That field is NOT a validated union at runtime: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:222` does `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` — a raw, unchecked cast of a Yorkie tree attribute, and `normalizeBlockStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:324) is just a spread over defaults, so it validates nothing. Attack: a collaborating peer (or anyone able to write the shared Yorkie doc / a crafted persisted document) sets the block attribute `alignment` to e.g. `center"/><w:r><w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"/></w:r><w:jc w:val="left`. When a victim exports that document to .docx, the injected markup lands verbatim in `word/document.xml`, letting the attacker synthesize arbitrary WordprocessingML (field codes, style refs, added runs) in a file the victim believes they authored. This is exactly the vector the delta cites in its own comments ("a peer's Yorkie attribute … never validated") when adding `escapeXmlAttr` to colors two lines below, so the fix is incomplete in the function it touches. Same file/function, one branch left unescaped.

verdict.reason: The claimed unescaped interpolation does not exist. At packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:166 the exporter does `const align = DOCX_ALIGNMENTS.get(style.alignment as string) ?? 'left'`, and only `align` — never `style.alignment` — is interpolated at line 168. DOCX_ALIGNMENTS (lines 118-123) is a closed 4-entry Map whose VALUES are the hardcoded ST_Jc tokens 'left'/'center'/'right'/'both'; an attacker payload like `center"/><w:r>...` is simply not a key, so `.get` returns undefined, `?? 'left'` fires, and the `align !== 'left'` guard drops the element. A Map rather than an object literal is used specifically so prototype keys (toString, constructor) cannot leak either (documented lines 111-116). Line 168 is the only `<w:jc w:val>` emission site in the source tree. The finding's cited evidence range (106-109) is not even the jc code — it is the tail of buildRunPropertiesXml. The claimed upstream "raw unchecked cast" is also absent: yorkie-doc-store.ts:222 is just `const parseBlockStyle = parseBlockStyleAttrs;`, and the real reader at crdt-attrs.ts:91 gates with the `isBlockAlignment` allowlist (crdt-attrs.ts:31-37), as does the writer at crdt-attrs.ts:66 and the content PUT API at docs-content.controller.ts:344-350 (with regression tests at docs-content.controller.spec.ts:514,582 firing this exact payload). The sink is structurally incapable of carrying attacker-chosen text.
